name: pyairbnb
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python client for Airbnb's unofficial API (search by location, listing details, user info, map visualization); does not explicitly document calendar/availability endpoints in its README, and ships no committed dataset — queries Airbnb live. 19 commits.
why_useful: A ready-made client-side hook into Airbnb's own (undocumented) API surface, which is what a calendar/availability puller would build on; flagged as a scraper of airbnb.com itself, which per repo rules is a terms-of-service call for a human, not to be run.
themes: Airbnb calendar / availability / blocked-night datasets and occupancy-estimation code (San Francisco model, review-to-booking ratios)
why_all: A ready-made client-side hook into Airbnb's own (undocumented) API surface, which is what a calendar/availability puller would build on; flagged as a scraper of airbnb.com itself, which per repo rules is a terms-of-service call for a human, not to be run.

name: cityofaustin/atd-utils-socrata
what_it_holds: Official City of Austin (Transportation Dept) Python utilities for interacting with the Socrata Open Data API generically (not STR-specific), public-domain licensed.
why_useful: A vetted, official client for pulling any Austin Socrata dataset including the STR licence dataset we already hold; useful as the maintained access method rather than a new API client, and could be adapted city-to-city since most of the target cities (Chicago, Seattle, Denver, etc.) also run Socrata portals (gap #17).
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold Austin daily STR licences per CONTEXT.md; this is just the access-library, not new data
themes: Municipal short-term-rental licence and registration datasets (Austin, LA HSO, SF OSTR, Denver, New Orleans, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, Honolulu) mirrored or pulled by code
why_all: A vetted, official client for pulling any Austin Socrata dataset including the STR licence dataset we already hold; useful as the maintained access method rather than a new API client, and could be adapted city-to-city since most of the target cities (Chicago, Seattle, Denver, etc.) also run Socrata portals (gap #17).

name: dolmios/airindex-2022
what_it_holds: Landing page/project 'AirIndex' described as testing techniques for aggregating and providing open short-term rental data from Airbnb (project site referenced, not the repo itself). README does not detail specific fields, and no data files are evident; appears to be a marketing/landing-page repo (Next.js tooling, sitemap generation) rather than a working data pipeline.
why_useful: Possible alternative acquisition method for Airbnb-adjacent open data aggregation; unverified maturity, low confidence without deeper inspection.
themes: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
Data-hosting mirrors pointed at from GitHub: Zenodo, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse, HuggingFace, Kaggle, Mendeley Data collections on Airbnb, STR, hotels, tourism
University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)
why_all: Possible alternative acquisition method for Airbnb-adjacent open data aggregation; unverified maturity, low confidence without deeper inspection.

Concept is on-theme (an open Airbnb data aggregation index) but content/status could not be confirmed as functional or as holding real data; flagging in case the live site (airindex site referenced in repo) has since published something.

Concept-stage aggregator for open STR data — flagged for completeness only; archived and undocumented, likely dead. Worth a 5-minute check of the live Vercel URL if someone wants to rule it out definitively.

name: how-to-scrape-airbnb (Oxylabs)
what_it_holds: Vendor (Oxylabs) tutorial repo (21 commits) using their paid Web Scraper API plus Python asyncio/aiohttp to pull Airbnb listing titles, nightly/total pricing, host URL, rating, review text/dates, and photos from both listing pages and paginated search results (up to 250 listings/search). No committed dataset.
why_useful: Documents Airbnb's current (2026) search-response JSON schema in a vendor-neutral tutorial form -- useful as a schema reference even without adopting Oxylabs' proxy product.
themes: Airbnb API wrappers and search-page clients (catalogue only, never run): pyairbnb, airbnb-scraper, airbnb search results parsers; note what fields they expose
Airbnb corporate open source (airbnb org) and public data pipelines built on Airbnb-internal-style data; Airbnb Data Science blog notebooks; Airbnb Newsroom scrapers
why_all: Documents Airbnb's current (2026) search-response JSON schema in a vendor-neutral tutorial form -- useful as a schema reference even without adopting Oxylabs' proxy product.
Another independent field-schema reference, but requires a paid third-party proxy/API service (Oxylabs), which is a heavier dependency than pyairbnb/gobnb which hit Airbnb directly.

Could theoretically extend the fee-panel search-page capture the team already runs (gap #2, realised/asking price), but it scrapes airbnb.com directly beyond the sanctioned capture and needs a paid proxy backend — a ToS decision, catalogue-only per repo rules, do not run.

name: api-evangelist/hostaway
what_it_holds: Same author's documentation profile of the Hostaway PMS public API surface (properties, reservations, channel management, revenue optimization endpoints). No data.
why_useful: Marginal: shows Hostaway exposes per-operator reservation/rate data, but only for a user's own connected account, not a market-wide benchmark — not useful for macro nowcasting.
themes: Property-management / channel-manager / PMS public data (Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Hostfully, Smoobu, Beds24, iCal feeds) and vacation-rental manager benchmarks
why_all: Marginal: shows Hostaway exposes per-operator reservation/rate data, but only for a user's own connected account, not a market-wide benchmark — not useful for macro nowcasting.
